Dana's skipping speed is 3 mph. Skipping is half as fast as running, so running speed is \(3 \times 2 = 6\) mph. Running is four times faster than walking, so walking speed is \(6 \div 4 = 1.5\) mph.

In six hours, she spends one-third of the time running: \(\frac{1}{3} \times 6 = 2\) hours running.  
She spends two-thirds of the time walking: \(\frac{2}{3} \times 6 = 4\) hours walking.

Distance running: \(6 \text{ mph} \times 2 \text{ hours} = 12\) miles.  
Distance walking: \(1.5 \text{ mph} \times 4 \text{ hours} = 6\) miles.  
Total distance: \(12 + 6 = 18\) miles.

Answer: 18
